known: A neuron reading is countable and repeatable. Batman has a core of units that no random set of 32 films has.

Heredity can be measured. With every name removed, adaptations carry their source comic's content (p = 0.0026 and 0.00017). The pattern holds in 99.6% of 30,240 analysis variants across both models and both text versions.
Word counts measure it just as well. On the primary model, words matched or beat neurons on every pre-registered test that had a word comparator.
Agreement between two companies' models is mostly shared name and word detectors. It collapses when names are removed.
A handful of units do behave like ideas: a funeral, a coin flip, the secret identity, and one revenge unit that picked the right sentence in 10 of 12 pairs with no revenge words.

Outside this project, the evidence is that neurons are a sparser basis than random directions, that in one 35B model about two thirds of neuron poles have one job or one dominant job at strong activation (Goodfire's companion paper of 10 November, graded by an LLM), that 1 to 5% of neurons recur across retrained models, and that plain prompting beats activation methods at steering text on the one large benchmark.

The field's own survey of November 2026 treats learned features, not neurons, as the default unit, and calls superposition a hypothesis in large models. On agreement between models it finds shared algorithms supported and shared representations fragile.
unknown: Whether neuron units follow an idea when the wording changes. This is the claim that would justify the method, and it has never been tested at scale, here or in Goodfire's companion paper.
Whether the units cause anything. Nobody in this project has turned a neuron up or down.

Whether the small 4-bit models used here are 'clean' at all. The two audits behind the claim, the essay's and its companion paper's, are of models four times larger, and the paper covers only each neuron's strongest 3% of firings.

Whether the dense 8B models used here run on their strongest neuron firings, as Goodfire's 35B model does. Earlier work on dense models could remove about half of all activations, not nine tenths. If these models are no sparser, reading only the strong range is not justified for them.
Whether a learned map between models carries concept units across. Only one-to-one twins were tried.
Whether neurons beat sentence embeddings or an LLM simply reading the text. Those rivals were never run, here or in Goodfire's companion paper.
Whether any human agrees with the labels. Every labeller, judge and reviewer so far was an AI.
Everything about selection, forecasting, editing and practical use. One underpowered test is all there is.
next: IN-29, UN-21 and IN-21: about a week on the laptop. A one-day check that 4-bit readings match full precision. A held-out count of twin neurons between Qwen and Llama on the 1,000 film plots already in the repository. Minimal pairs for 30 story concepts, with decoys that use the words without the idea.

EN-21 and CE-21: three or four days. Push the 31 named units while the model writes and see whether blind judges get the label back. Test units against human coders of what people kept when retelling a story.
IN-24 and UN-23. Is a meme one neuron, a few neurons or a direction? Does a map fitted on paired text carry a reading from Qwen to Llama?
IN-25 and UN-22, on one download. Do two summaries of the same story give the same reading, and does the reading survive a change of language?
RX-27: about three days. The first use test. Name a known source after deep rewording, against look-alike decoys. A pass opens the family-tree designs RX-22 and LI-22.

Before any of it, write down which results would move the unit from single neurons to small sets or directions. Start no lineage, forecasting or product design until a frozen unit has beaten sentence embeddings and an LLM reader on text where the words are controlled.

news.title: Neurons as an Interpretable Basis
news.kind: Goodfire research post, not peer reviewed
news.by: Tigges, Kowal, McGrath, Lewis and Cammarata
news.what: The technical companion to the essay behind premise P1. It studies one model, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which sends each token to a few of 256 sub-networks per layer.
points: Strong firings carry the computation. Zeroing the weakest 92.2% of the activations in play at each token raises loss by 2.9%. Keeping a random eighth, or removing only the strongest eighth, more than doubles it. Most reasoning and knowledge benchmarks fall until the model is fine-tuned.

One job is the majority, not the rule. Of 5,468 neuron poles, 47% have one role and 69% have one role doing at least 90% of the damage when the neuron is removed. The essay had said about 90%, for a different model.

A short description predicts strong firing. A judge given the description picks the passage where the neuron fires 95% of the time against random text and 89% against text sent to the same sub-network. Chance is 50%.

It does not test what this programme needs. No word-count or embedding rival is scored, no measured test removes an idea's usual words, no statistic is repeated on a second model, and nothing is at the level of a whole document.
news.changes: For the programme: read each unit only in its own strong range, record which of its roles fired, and treat a label as a guess until it predicts held-out firings. Fifteen designs were amended and four were registered to carry the paper's tests over to the study's own models, with the rivals it left out.

news.title: Understanding AI from the Inside
news.by: Barez, Wu and 25 co-authors, among them Yoshua Bengio
news.what: A survey of mechanistic interpretability, the field that studies what happens inside models. It was posted five days before Goodfire's paper and does not cite the essay. Most of it is about AI safety.
points: Its default unit is the feature, usually found with a learned dictionary, not the neuron. It says single neurons often mix unrelated concepts at strong activation, and gives no rate.
It concedes two points to the neuron side. Superposition is 'a hypothesis, not an established fact' in large language models, and the neurons of an MLP block are a privileged basis.
On agreement between models it is compatible with this roadmap. Shared algorithms are supported. Shared internal representations are 'less supported', and the similarity scores behind them 'fragile'.

Its test for a label is causal: change the unit and see the output move, against random units of matched size. Its protocol sets baselines before the method is run: random directions, principal components, single neurons and supervised probes.
news.changes: For the programme: the survey's standards cover part of the validation ladder and add two things it lacked, a statement of coverage and a swap test. It has no test that a reading follows an idea and not a word. Ten designs were amended and three registered.
